interest: This file provides rare insight into bureaucratic tensions between Washington and SCAP over educational authority, particularly General MacArthur’s insistence on military control over civilian commissioners. It uniquely juxtaposes high-level pedagogical planning with grassroots enthusiasm from American educators, while preserving comprehensive bibliographies that reveal the precise cultural materials selected to reshape post-war Japanese society.
keywords: United States Education Mission to Japan
overview: This file documents the planning, dispatch, reception, and policy implementation of the 1946 United States Education Mission to Japan, organized by the Department of State and the War Department at the request of the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP). It encompasses high-level interagency coordination, candidate selection, and personal reflections from mission members under George D. Stoddard regarding democratic educational reconstruction and language reform. The collection also captures debates over administrative oversight and the rejection of an independent civilian educational commissioner in favor of SCAP's Civil Information and Education Section, alongside numerous unsolicited applications from American teachers—including Nisei educators—seeking occupation service. Finally, the records detail public outreach campaigns, the distribution of the Mission's report, extensive bibliographies of American children's and adult literature shipped to Japanese schools to foster democratic values, and a 1949 review of the Japanese civics textbook Primer of Democracy.
